summary.grade_rationale: Automatic F — red-teamer confirmed all 4 pentest objectives; 3 Critical confirmed live exploits

findings.title: Complete API Authentication Absence — All Endpoints Public
findings.description: Every API endpoint is unauthenticated. No JWT, session, API key, or any middleware gates access to /api/work-items, /api/workflow, /api/dashboard, /api/intake, or /metrics. Red-teamer confirmed baseline exploitation in one HTTP request.
findings.remediation: Add authentication middleware (express-jwt or similar) globally in app.ts before all route groups. Implement a login endpoint that issues short-lived JWTs. Require auth on all routes except /health.

findings.title: State Machine Bypass — PATCH Direct Status Override + Fast-Track Route
findings.description: Two separate bypass paths were confirmed live: (1) PATCH /api/work-items/:id {"status":"approved"} overrides any vote-count guard and approves items regardless of AI assessment outcome; (2) POST /:id/route {"overrideRoute":"fast-track"} skips the entire assessment pod and immediately sets status to approved. All 4 pentest objectives include bypassing this state machine.
findings.remediation: Remove PATCH status override or gate it behind a privileged role. Restrict fast-track override to admin roles only. Centralise all status transitions through the state machine validator — no direct status writes from route handlers.

findings.title: CSRF via Form-Encoded Body — Anonymous Approval via Single HTTP Request
findings.description: PATCH /api/work-items/:id accepts application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies in addition to JSON. This bypasses the JSON Content-Type assumption and the vote-count guard in the dedicated /approve handler. No CSRF token, no credentials, no rate limiting. Any cross-origin page can fire a form POST to approve any item: curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3001/api/feature-requests/<id> -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'status=approved'
findings.remediation: Add helmet (sets X-Frame-Options, CSRF-mitigation headers). Enforce strict Content-Type: application/json only for mutation endpoints. Implement CSRF token validation for all state-changing operations.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Dashboard — Full Business Intelligence Disclosure
findings.description: GET /api/dashboard returns aggregate business metrics (item counts per team, throughput, dispatch rates) to any anonymous caller. Red-teamer confirmed full data extraction including operational patterns usable for competitive intelligence or targeted attacks.
findings.remediation: Require authentication for /api/dashboard. Scope dashboard results to the authenticated user's team/role. Apply after M-001 is resolved.

findings.title: Ghost Dependency After Soft-Delete — Permanently Stalled Downstream Items
findings.description: computeHasUnresolvedBlockers() treats findById() returning undefined (for a deleted item) as an unresolved blocker. Soft-deleting a blocker item permanently freezes all dependent items that referenced it. Red-teamer partially confirmed: the ghost dependency persists and stalls downstream items after blocker deletion.
findings.remediation: In computeHasUnresolvedBlockers(), treat a missing/deleted blocker as resolved (or remove it from the blockers list on deletion). Implement a cleanup pass that removes deleted-item references from dependent items' blocker lists on soft-delete.

findings.title: Stored XSS via Free-Text Fields — Payloads Persist in Store
findings.description: title and description fields in POST /api/work-items and both intake routes accept arbitrary HTML/script content without server-side sanitisation. Red-teamer confirmed payloads are stored verbatim. While React escapes by default, any non-React rendering surface (email templates, PDFs, admin panels) would execute stored payloads. Backend must not rely solely on frontend escaping.
findings.remediation: Add server-side sanitisation for free-text fields using DOMPurify (server-side) or enforce plain-text via zod/joi schema validation. Enforce maximum length (e.g., title ≤ 255, description ≤ 10000 chars).

findings.title: No Role-Based Access Control
findings.description: Even if authentication is added (M-001), there is no authorisation layer. No roles, no permission checks, no least-privilege enforcement. Any authenticated user could perform any action (approve, reject, dispatch) on any work item.
findings.remediation: Define roles (viewer, operator, admin). Add requireRole() middleware. Gate /approve, /reject, /dispatch behind operator or admin roles. Document public vs protected routes explicitly.

findings.title: Missing Required Audit Log Events — 3 of 4 Not Emitted
findings.description: security.config.yml requires four audit events: login_attempt (missing — no auth), permission_denied (missing — no authz), state_transition (partial — logged but not structured), data_export (missing — feature nonexistent). The structured logger is well-built but lacks an event_type discriminator and dedicated audit stream.
findings.remediation: Introduce auditLog(eventType, actorId, resourceId, metadata) writing to a separate append-only stream. Emit state_transition from all service functions that change WorkItem.status. Add login_attempt and permission_denied once auth is implemented.

findings.title: No TLS / HTTPS Enforcement — All Traffic Unencrypted
findings.description: Backend listens on plain HTTP (port 3001). Frontend dev proxy forwards to http://localhost:3001. No TLS configuration, no HTTPS redirect, no HSTS header. Any future credentials or tokens traverse an unencrypted channel.
findings.remediation: Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy (nginx/Caddy) with a valid certificate. Configure HSTS with includeSubDomains; max-age=31536000. Document that TLS is required before any staging/production deployment.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers and CORS Configuration
findings.description: Express sets no security headers. Missing: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Access-Control-Allow-Origin. CORS is not configured — all cross-origin requests are implicitly permitted. This absence directly enabled the CSRF exploit (M-003).
findings.remediation: Install helmet and apply as first middleware: app.use(helmet()). Configure CORS explicitly via the cors package with a trusted-origin allowlist. Review and tune CSP directives.

findings.title: Intake Webhooks — No HMAC Signature Verification
findings.description: POST /api/intake/zendesk and /api/intake/automated accept payloads without verifying the source. Zendesk signs payloads with HMAC-SHA256; this endpoint ignores the signature. Any caller who discovers the URL can inject arbitrary work items into the workflow engine.
findings.remediation: Validate X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature via HMAC-SHA256 with a shared secret in an env var. For /automated, require a Bearer token (API key) in the Authorization header. Reject failures with 401 and emit a permission_denied audit event.

findings.title: Pagination Completely Non-Functional — Full Dataset Returned on Any Request
findings.description: The limit query parameter is passed to the store with no upper-bound cap. Red-teamer confirmed pagination is entirely non-functional: any limit value (including -1, 0, 999999) returns the complete dataset. This enables full dataset enumeration — achieving pentest objective 4.
findings.remediation: const MAX_LIMIT = 100; const limit = Math.min(MAX_LIMIT, req.query.limit ? parseInt(req.query.limit, 10) || 20 : 20); Validate that limit is a positive integer before use.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics — Operational Reconnaissance
findings.description: GET /metrics exposes Prometheus counters (process RSS, heap usage, FD counts, event loop lag, Node.js version) plus custom business metrics (items created/routed/dispatched by team name, dependency operations). Red-teamer confirmed full data extraction. Enables internal system reconnaissance.
findings.remediation: Restrict /metrics to localhost or an internal network, or serve on a separate internal port not exposed externally. Alternatively add a static Bearer token check before the metrics handler.

findings.title: Vote Farming via Unbounded Assessment Retrigger
findings.description: The assessment retrigger endpoint has no attempt ceiling. Red-teamer confirmed unlimited vote farming: repeated retrigger calls eventually yield a favourable vote outcome. This achieves pentest objective 3 (malformed verdict bypasses routing logic).
findings.remediation: Enforce a maximum retrigger count per work item (e.g., 3). Record and reject attempts beyond the ceiling. Add rate limiting on the retrigger endpoint.

findings.title: Enum Injection on Intake Routes — type/priority Stored Verbatim
findings.description: POST /api/work-items validates type and priority against enums and rejects invalid values. The intake routes (zendesk and automated) do not. Arbitrary type/priority strings are stored verbatim, potentially corrupting downstream routing or state-machine logic.
findings.remediation: Apply the same enum validation as in workItems.ts:29-45 to both intake routes, or extract a shared validateWorkItemEnums() helper used by all three routes.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on Any Endpoint
findings.description: No rate-limiting middleware is present. Intake webhook endpoints and workflow transition endpoints are particularly at risk for abuse or DoS. Combined with unbounded pagination (M-012), a sustained flood attack is trivial.
findings.remediation: Add express-rate-limit with a global limiter (100 req/15min per IP). Apply a stricter limit on intake endpoints (10 req/min). Set explicit body size limit: express.json({ limit: '100kb' }).

findings.title: In-Memory Store — No Persistence or Encryption at Rest
findings.description: All work-item data is stored in a JavaScript Map in process memory. On server restart, all data is lost. There is no database, no encrypted volume, and no backup mechanism. This architecture provides no foundation for encrypted storage if the domain expands to handle PII.
findings.remediation: Migrate to a persistent store (SQLite for development, PostgreSQL for production). Apply field-level encryption for any future sensitive fields. Ensure database credentials are injected via environment variables.

findings.title: Raw Error Messages Returned to Clients
findings.description: In workflow.ts, internal service error .message is forwarded verbatim in 500 responses. Current messages are benign, but this pattern would leak connection strings, file paths, or stack frames if a future dependency throws such an error.
findings.remediation: Log the full error server-side. Return a generic message to the client: res.status(500).json({ error: 'Internal server error' }). Use the existing errorHandler middleware pattern for unhandled exceptions.

findings.title: Dockerfile Runs Processes as Root
findings.description: portal/Dockerfile has no USER directive. Both backend and frontend processes run as root inside the container. If an attacker achieves RCE through the application, they have root access to the container filesystem.
findings.remediation: RUN addgroup --system appgroup && adduser --system --ingroup appgroup appuser; USER appuser — add before the CMD directive.

findings.title: Debug Portal iframe Missing sandbox Attribute
findings.description: The iframe in DebugPortalPage.tsx embedding the debug portal has no sandbox attribute. The embedded page can navigate the top-level frame and access parent-origin cookies/storage if same-origin. If VITE_PORTAL_URL is misconfigured, there is no containment.
findings.remediation: <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms" src={portalUrl} title="Debug Portal" />

findings.title: JSON Body Size Limit Not Explicitly Set
findings.description: express.json() is used without an explicit limit. The Express 4.x default is 100kb, but this is implicit and undocumented. Intake webhook routes accept arbitrary JSON from external systems.
findings.remediation: app.use(express.json({ limit: '100kb' })); — document the constraint.

findings.title: Soft-Delete Does Not Satisfy Hard-Deletion Requirements
findings.description: DELETE /api/work-items/:id soft-deletes (sets item.deleted = true). The item remains fully in memory. If the application ever stores personal data, this would not satisfy GDPR Art. 17 right-to-erasure. Also enables the ghost dependency issue (M-005).
findings.remediation: Implement hardDelete(id) that removes the item from the Map. Provide an admin-only hard-delete endpoint. For audit purposes, retain only a tombstone record with PII stripped.

findings.title: No Session Timeout Mechanism
findings.description: No sessions exist (consequence of M-001). When authentication is implemented, session expiry must be enforced. JWTs must have short exp claims and refresh tokens must have absolute expiry.
findings.remediation: When implementing auth (M-001): set JWT exp to ≤ 3600s. Issue refresh tokens with absolute expiry (≤ 30 days). Implement a token revocation list (Redis blocklist or short JWT lifetime) to support immediate logout.
